physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the pineal gland, the small pinecone-shaped body buried deep in the centre of the brain, the one piece of nervous tissue that sits alone on the midline instead of paired left and right. It is the gland that reads light and dark for the whole body, the inner clock, and the old anatomists called it the seat of the soul long before anyone knew what it did. It is fitting that the last of the sixty-four codes, the one that ends on illumination, sits in the organ that already speaks in the language of light.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. When the days fog over and nothing in the mind will settle, the pressure is felt high inside the head, behind the eyes and above them, a held, swirling weight where the gland sits. Sleep goes shallow. The inner clock loses its sense of when. The body knows a transformation is wanting to come through, and the gland is straining to catch a signal that has not arrived yet.

The climb out is also bodily, and it is quiet. The pressure unwinds. Sleep gets deep again, and dreams come back in colour. There are small flashes of an inward brightness that has nothing to do with the eyes, behind the brow, sometimes for no reason. The gland is not making the light. It is the part of the body that finally stops blocking it.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to a single amino acid, Glycine. Glycine is the smallest letter in the whole alphabet the body writes with, the simplest of all the twenty, a single carbon between two hands. It is also one of the brain's quieting agents, an inhibitory signal that tells a firing neuron to settle, to slow, to stop.

There is a teaching in that, and it lands at the centre of this card. The code whose shadow is the racing, scrambling mind runs on the chemistry of stillness. The smallest letter in the body is also the one that says hush. Confusion was never going to be solved by another thought added on top. It was going to be ended by a chemistry already inside you, asking the noise to come down a notch and then a notch more, until there is room for something else to arrive.

The code runs all the way to this: a fog that lifts not by adding light, but by letting the body's own quieting reach the place that was making the storm.
